files.README.md:
# Catalog cache
`Catalog.put(id, title)` creates or updates a product; `delete(id)` removes it.
`CatalogCache.get(id)` returns a product dict or None. Reads may be cached, but
after a put or delete the next read of that id must be fresh. Edits to one id
must not cause a database read for another cached id. `Catalog.reads` counts
database reads and is public for diagnostics. Changing a returned dict must
not change a later cached read.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

from catalog.store import Catalog
from catalog.cache import CatalogCache

def debug_test():
    # Create a catalog and cache
    catalog = Catalog()
    cache = CatalogCache(catalog)
    
    print("Initial state:")
    print(f"Catalog versions: {catalog.versions}")
    print(f"Cache versions: {cache.versions}")
    print(f"Cache entries: {cache.entries}")
    
    # Put some data
    print("\nPutting item 1...")
    catalog.put(1, "Product 1")
    print(f"After put - Catalog versions: {catalog.versions}")
    print(f"After put - Cache versions: {cache.versions}")
    print(f"After put - Cache entries: {cache.entries}")
    
    # Read item 
    print("\nReading item 1...")
    item = cache.get(1)
    print(f"Read result: {item}")
    print(f"After read - Catalog versions: {catalog.versions}")
    print(f"After read - Cache versions: {cache.versions}")
    print(f"After read - Cache entries: {cache.entries}")
    
    # Modify the returned dictionary
    print("\nModifying returned item...")
    original_title = item['title']
    item['title'] = "Modified Title"
    print(f"After modification - Modified item title: {item['title']}")
    print(f"Original title was: {original_title}")
    
    # Read again
    print("\nReading item 1 again...")
    item2 = cache.get(1)
    print(f"Second read result: {item2}")
    print(f"After second read - Catalog versions: {catalog.versions}")
    print(f"After second read - Cache versions: {cache.versions}")
    print(f"After second read - Cache entries: {cache.entries}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    debug_test()

#!/usr/bin/env python3

from catalog.store import Catalog
from catalog.cache import CatalogCache

def test_final():
    # Create a catalog and cache
    catalog = Catalog()
    cache = CatalogCache(catalog)
    
    print("1. Test basic functionality")
    catalog.put(1, "Product 1")
    
    # First read - should be cached
    item1 = cache.get(1)
    print(f"First read: {item1}")
    assert item1['title'] == "Product 1"
    
    print("\n2. Test update invalidates cache")
    catalog.put(1, "Updated Product 1")
    
    # Second read - should be fresh (not cached)
    item1_updated = cache.get(1)
    print(f"After update: {item1_updated}")
    assert item1_updated['title'] == "Updated Product 1"
    
    print("\n3. Test delete invalidates cache")
    catalog.delete(1)
    
    # Read after delete - should be None and fresh
    item1_deleted = cache.get(1)
    print(f"After delete: {item1_deleted}")
    assert item1_deleted is None
    
    print("\n4. Test that other cached entries unaffected")
    catalog.put(2, "Product 2") 
    catalog.put(3, "Product 3")
    
    # Cache items
    item2 = cache.get(2)
    item3 = cache.get(3)
    print(f"Cached items: {item2}, {item3}")
    
    # Update item 2 - should not affect item 3 caching
    catalog.put(2, "Updated Product 2")
    item2_after_update = cache.get(2)
    item3_after_update = cache.get(3) 
    
    print(f"Item 2 after update: {item2_after_update}")
    print(f"Item 3 after update (should still be cached): {item3_after_update}")
    
    assert item2_after_update['title'] == "Updated Product 2"
    assert item3_after_update['title'] == "Product 3"
    
    print("\n5. Test that database reads counter works")
    initial_reads = catalog.reads
    cache.get(1)  # This should increase reads
    cache.get(2)  # This should increase reads 
    final_reads = catalog.reads
    print(f"Database reads went from {initial_reads} to {final_reads}")
    
    print("\n✅ All requirements satisfied!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_final()

#!/usr/bin/env python3

from catalog.store import Catalog
from catalog.cache import CatalogCache

def test_cache_invalidation():
    # Create a catalog and cache
    catalog = Catalog()
    cache = CatalogCache(catalog)
    
    print("=== Test 1: Basic cached read ===")
    catalog.put(1, "Product 1")
    
    item1 = cache.get(1)
    print(f"First read: {item1}")
    assert item1['title'] == "Product 1"
    
    print("\n=== Test 2: Modify returned dict (not affecting cache) ===")
    item1['title'] = "Modified Title"
    item1_again = cache.get(1)  # Should still return original
    print(f"Second read after modifying returned: {item1_again}")
    assert item1_again['title'] == "Product 1"  # This assertion may be violated due to copy behavior
    
    print("\n=== Test 3: Update item and verify cache is invalidated ===")
    catalog.put(1, "Updated Product 1") 
    item1_updated = cache.get(1)
    print(f"After update, read: {item1_updated}")
    assert item1_updated['title'] == "Updated Product 1"
    
    # Verify that other cached entries aren't affected
    print("\n=== Test 4: Other entries still cached ===")
    catalog.put(2, "Product 2")
    item2 = cache.get(2)
    print(f"Read item 2: {item2}")
    
    # Update item 1 again to make sure we're not affecting other entries
    catalog.put(1, "Updated Again Product 1")
    item1_again2 = cache.get(1)
    assert item1_again2['title'] == "Updated Again Product 1"
    
    item2_again = cache.get(2) 
    assert item2_again['title'] == "Product 2"  # Should still be cached
    
    print("\n=== Test 5: Delete entry ===")
    catalog.delete(2)
    item2_deleted = cache.get(2)
    assert item2_deleted is None
    
    print("All tests completed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_cache_invalidation()

#!/usr/bin/env python3

from catalog.store import Catalog
from catalog.cache import CatalogCache

def test_read_counter():
    catalog = Catalog()
    cache = CatalogCache(catalog)
    
    print(f"Initial reads: {catalog.reads}")
    
    # Put items
    catalog.put(1, "Product 1")
    print(f"After put 1: {catalog.reads}")
    
    # First read - should cause a database read
    item1 = cache.get(1)
    print(f"After first get 1: {catalog.reads}")
    
    # Second read of same item - should be cached
    item1_again = cache.get(1)
    print(f"After second get 1: {catalog.reads}")
    
    # Update the item
    catalog.put(1, "Updated Product 1")
    print(f"After update 1: {catalog.reads}")
    
    # Get again - should be fresh 
    item1_updated = cache.get(1)
    print(f"After get updated 1: {catalog.reads}")
    
    print("✅ Read counter test completed")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_read_counter()

#!/usr/bin/env python3

from catalog.store import Catalog
from catalog.cache import CatalogCache

def test_cache():
    # Create a catalog and cache
    catalog = Catalog()
    cache = CatalogCache(catalog)
    
    # Put some data
    catalog.put(1, "Product 1")
    catalog.put(2, "Product 2")
    
    # Read first item - should be cached
    item1 = cache.get(1)
    assert item1['title'] == "Product 1"
    
    # Read second item - should be cached
    item2 = cache.get(2)
    assert item2['title'] == "Product 2"
    
    # Update first item
    catalog.put(1, "Updated Product 1")
    
    # Read first item again - should be fresh (not cached)
    item1_updated = cache.get(1)
    assert item1_updated['title'] == "Updated Product 1"
    
    # Second item should still be cached  
    item2_again = cache.get(2)
    assert item2_again['title'] == "Product 2"
    
    # Delete item
    catalog.delete(2)
    
    # Read deleted item - should be None and fresh
    item2_deleted = cache.get(2)
    assert item2_deleted is None
    
    # Read still-existing item - should still be cached
    item1_again = cache.get(1)
    assert item1_again['title'] == "Updated Product 1"
    
    print("All tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_cache()

from catalog.store import Catalog
from catalog.cache import CatalogCache

def test_modification():
    # Create a catalog and cache
    catalog = Catalog()
    cache = CatalogCache(catalog)
    
    # Put some data
    catalog.put(1, "Product 1")
    
    # Read item
    item = cache.get(1)
    assert item['title'] == "Product 1"
    
    # Modify the returned dictionary
    item['title'] = "Modified Title"
    
    # Read again - should be original value, not modified
    item2 = cache.get(1)
    assert item2['title'] == "Product 1"
    
    print("Modification test passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_modification()
